messages:
emma: quick follow-up from the spike — instead of full per-tenant control plane split or heavy peering, i'm proposing a minimal sidecar contract that delegates identity + routing decisions to the control plane but keeps a single shared cp. idea is to avoid NAT/ip-mapping churn while giving tenants an auditable identity header.

emma: sketch: sidecar authenticates to CP, receives a short-lived 'egress-identity' token per request, and injects it as a header to provider endpoints. no SNAT, no per-tenant vpcs required. example header:```
X-Redwood-Egress-Identity: tenant=tenant-42;role=ingress;exp=1710003600;sig=MEUCIQD...
```

raj: high-level — i like avoiding per-tenant ip accounting. couple quick concerns: 1) downstream services often rely on source IP for rate-limiting + geo. 2) how do we preserve k8s NetworkPolicy / security groups semantics?

maria: +1 on auditability. if we sign the token via KMS key per-tenant, downstream can verify and log tenant without needing separate network paths. that handles the logging concern but not ip-based rate limits.

sam: for rate limits, we could put an internal proxy/edge that consumes X-Redwood-Egress-Identity and enforces token-based quotas. that lets downstream ignore source IP for multi-tenant stuff.

emma: exactly — two levers: preserve ip (opt-in via per-tenant egress) or switch consumers to token-based auth. migration plan would be phased: 1) token injection + audit logs, 2) consumer opt-in to token enforcement, 3) optional per-tenant egress for legacy consumers.

emma: tradeoffs i called out in the spike notes:
- pros: simpler infra, fewer peering/NAT routes, faster rollout for new tenants, central observability of identities
- cons: requires consumer changes for ip-based policies, needs robust token signing/rotation, slightly more trust surface in sidecar/CP link

raj: what about replay or token theft? can we bind token to flow? maybe include src-ip or tcp-socket-id inside the signed payload so token can't be reused from another host.

maria: or issue tokens scoped to a single downstream TLS session id. but that gets messy with connection reuse. src-ip binding is reasonable for short TTL (30s).

sam: ops/mea: key management questions — do we want one global signing key or per-tenant keys? per-tenant gives better audit/rotation granularity but increases KMS calls.

emma: leaning per-tenant keys but using a cached signer in CP to avoid per-request KMS ops. expiration short (30-60s) reduces blast radius. also record signing events for audit.

ops-bot: deploy pipeline: sidecar-contract-v1 image built (sha: a1b2c3). smoke tests queued. :rocket:

raj: operational concern: debugging will need a way to correlate token -> tenant without hitting KMS for every verification. include token metadata in logs (sig id, key id) so we can map offline.

maria: also add a fallback header X-Redwood-Egress-Method: token|snat so downstream can distinguish.

emma: good call. i'll add that to the interface.

sam: can we sketch failure modes? e.g., if CP unavailable the sidecar should either: a) fail closed (reject new egress), b) fall back to per-node SNAT if allowed. ops needs a flag.

emma: propose default fail-open to node SNAT for now (to keep customer apps alive) but with a strong ops alert and automatic transition to fail-closed for high-security tenants. we'll make it configurable per-tenant.

maria: i'll draft an RFC addendum with: interface spec, token format, key mgmt, migration path, and failure-mode matrix. can we get a quick review tomorrow?

emma: yes. @raj @sam — can you skim the token payload draft i posted and flag anything missing? i'll include the verification flow and metrics we should emit (token-issue-count, verify-latency, failover-count).

raj: will do. +1 for starting with token-first approach and keeping per-tenant egress as an escape hatch.

sam: adding a note: update the console to surface token-based errors and per-tenant failover counts so support can triage.

emma: awesome. i'll drop the RFC link in this thread once i finish the doc. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
